formation.explanation: Apply admission reaches the leader main loop, which assigns term/index and stores logs before reporting self support. Per-peer replication sends bounded batches with previous index/term, retries rejected prefixes and falls back to snapshots for missing history. Follower append persists nonduplicate entries before success. The leader-lifetime commitment tracker counts only current voters, advances at a majority index only after the first entry of this term is supported, and notifies the main loop. That loop advances commit/configuration state and enqueues committed tuples for runFSM; FSM application supplies command responses. Replication CommitTimeout carries the leader commit frontier to idle followers; their processLogs path feeds the same serialized FSM consumer.

context.explanation: A follower without recent contact campaigns only if it is a voter. Per-attempt pre-vote/election channels isolate replies; real elections persist term and vote, and remote handlers enforce term, candidate eligibility, prior vote and log freshness. A winning majority creates a fresh leader commitment/replication lifetime and appends a current-term noop. Newer-term RPCs, replication rejection signals, voter-only lease loss or committed local removal can end leadership. Cleanup stops old workers and rejects pending futures; surviving old replies refer to old tracker/channel objects. Already enqueued FSM work has its own owner and may complete after stepdown. Persistent logs/snapshots and vote freshness carry prior decided history into later campaigns; new leaders collect fresh replication support.

connection.explanation: The authority context selects both the log that may be advanced and the eligible voters whose support can advance it. Membership is logged, normally one uncommitted change at a time, and updates the commitment voter set and replication workers immediately; followers roll back latest membership with a conflicting suffix. Elections compare retained log/snapshot history, while the current-term commitment threshold prevents using mere old-term support as fresh authority. Recovery reconstructs history and configuration before campaigning. Heartbeats confirm contact but carry no commit index; VerifyLeader consumes separate per-request callbacks and lease checks count recent voter contacts. Verification registration includes nonvoter replication workers despite a voter-derived threshold, retained as an unresolved eligibility question rather than a guarantee.

feedback.answered: The first backbone trace connects term-owned commitment, voter eligibility, replication, recovery and FSM completion. VerifyLeader initializes a voter-count threshold but registers the future on every nonlocal replication worker, and notifyAll supplies identity-free positive callbacks to the tally. No suffrage check appears on that inspected registration-to-completion path. Voter-only commitment and lease enforcement are distinct protections and remain contrary evidence against a broader claim that nonvoters generally form consensus.
